agent.reason: Current evidence still does not satisfy CVS. C1 remains clearly unsatisfied: the gallbladder neck/infundibulum is only partly visible and two distinct tubular structures entering the gallbladder cannot be confidently distinguished; instrument/tissue occlusion further limits the entry-site view. C2 is improved but still unsatisfied: the hepatocystic triangle is only partially cleared, with residual fat/fibrous tissue still obscuring the interior and no decisive view of a fully cleared triangle. C3 is closest but incomplete: the lower third of the gallbladder appears partly detached, yet a tissue bridge persists and cystic plate exposure is not continuous. Given the strongest blockers are residual obscuration and incomplete dissection, the next safest progress is careful right-sided dissection toward the cystic plate while the left grasper improves exposure and the camera stabilizes on the hepatocystic triangle/lower gallbladder interface.

rationale.c1: The view shows inflamed Calot's region with one apparent duct-like tubular structure and surrounding tissue, but it is not possible to clearly confirm exactly two distinct tubular structures entering the gallbladder.
rationale.c2: There is substantial fat and fibrous tissue still present in the hepatocystic triangle, with no clear complete clearance visible.
rationale.c3: Only part of the gallbladder/cystic plate interface is exposed; the lower third does not appear fully detached in this frame.
